Synopsis:
Karlach goes to HoH for the first time.

Cluster Contexts:
- Karlach_InParty_Nested_BackInHell.json: Karlach is visiting the HoH for the first time — a place that touches on her past in the Hells and the betrayal that led to her infernal engine. She’s tense and triggered by the setting, using sarcasm and clipped threats to cover rising panic (“this is all your fault,” “you’re lucky I care about the fate of your eternal soul”). The player is acting as a calming presence, trying to keep her from losing control in a scene that can reopen old traumas (she was sold to a devil years ago and has long struggled with that history). Off-screen context: Karlach has adapted to life with an infernal engine and a complicated history with other companions, and the party’s recent abduction and the shared tadpole parasite are continuing background stresses.
- WYR_GortashConfrontation_SoulConsumption.json: After a difficult fight and defeating Gortash, Karlach stands over the battle and accepts - for the first time - that permadeath is coming for her.
- COL_Karlach_AvatarSawGortash.json: Karlach has a self-dialogue after defeating Ketheric in the Colony. This is also her first chance to reflect on seeing Gortash - she was NOT expecting to see him here. Because the moment right before this is very high-intensity, I wanted this Karlach moment to start low-intensity and ramp up from there.
- LOW_DevilsFee_RitualCircle.json: Dialog to invoke the ritual to go to House of Hope from Lower City.RELEVANT NOTE: This dialog will only appear at the first time players go to house of hope. Later, this never will be triggered again.
- Karlach_InPartyEND.json: The InParty for Karlach while in END_Main.Morphic Pool (Arrival)Astral Plane (Just after Netherbrain Confrontation)Tadpole Choice (with Emperor in Astral Plane while making the choice to transform into a mind flayer. Karlach can transform into a mind flayer)High Hall Interior (after Astral Plane, views of Nautiloids, Dragons, and a city in ruin)

context: Karlach is visiting the House of Hope for the first time, a place that directly echoes her past in the Hells and the betrayal that led to her being fitted with an infernal engine. She’s tense and easily triggered, using sarcasm and clipped threats to mask rising panic as memories and trauma resurface. The player character is acting as a calming presence, trying to keep her from losing control during this initial, emotionally fraught visit. Off-screen, Karlach has adapted to life with the engine and carries ongoing stresses from recent events (the party’s abduction and the shared tadpole parasite), and this conversation only appears the first time the player brings her to the House of Hope.
